papers.title: Addressing the data limitations of deep learning algorithms for the detection of marine mammal species in large acoustic datasets
papers.abstract: Bioacoustics, the study of animal sounds, is crucial for ecology and conservation. However, such studies are limited by the time required to process the thousands of hours of recordings they generate. While deep learning (DL) methods have emerged as a powerful solution for some acoustic detection tasks, the complexities of bioacoustics data often violate core assumptions of these models. Here, I present tools that translate DL advancements to real-world bioacoustics applications. First, I demonstrate that annotations made at the level of fixed intervals of a few minutes, rather than labelling each individual call, are not a limitation for training DL models. I design a framework that learns to identify sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) click trains (series of short, broadband, regularly spaced clicks) directly from 4-minute recordings without individual clicks labelled, achieving performance comparable to expert auditors. Building on this method, I systematically evaluate how well DL models transfer across recording and labelling conditions. Trained models dropped in performance when deployed on new data. However, pretraining on a large, diverse dataset and fine-tuning with a small selection of new data performed comparably to training on a large sample of the target dataset outright. Active learning, which selects the most informative recordings to audit and add to the training dataset, consistently outperformed all other tested transferability approaches. Finally, I introduce an approach for handling evolving call classification systems through a case study on humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) song units, the smallest components of their songs, designing an expert-in-the-loop framework that achieved performance comparable to full expert annotation on unseen years’ recordings with less than 10% of the expert annotation effort. Through these contributions, this thesis provides novel frameworks for overcoming key mismatches between bioacoustic data realities and DL requirements, addressing the annotation and processing bottleneck that limits bioacoustics studies.

papers.title: Cognitive Digital Ocean: integration of quantum hybrid computing, digital twins and graph neural networks for bioresource and fleet management. Part 2
papers.abstract: The paper presents the concept of the Cognitive Digital Ocean (CDO) – a multi level cyber physical system for managing the fishery complex, integrating quantum hybrid computing, physics informed neural networks (PINN), graph neural networks (GNN), a hierarchy of digital twins (from genome to global ocean), and fractal analysis of the spatial distribution of bioresources. Special attention is paid to the shipbuilding aspect: mathematical models of the ship power plant (SPP), controllable pitch propeller (CPP), propulsion complex, and hull hydrodynamics are presented. It is shown that solving the fundamental Millennium Problem – the Navier Stokes equations – on quantum computers opens up fundamental possibilities for hydrodynamic forecasting with a horizon of up to 30 days. The system is aimed at solving the strategic tasks of the Russian Federal Agency for Fisheries (Rosrybolovstvo) until 2030: increasing production by 25%, digital transformation, and technological sovereignty. The limitations of the applicability of quantum methods are considered and engineering workarounds are proposed.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Intelligent Fiber Sensors: From Physical Design Optimization to Advanced Sensing Applications
papers.abstract: Fiber sensors encompass optical-fiber platforms and electrically functional fibers, yarns, and textiles that produce spectral, temporal, and spatial data across wearable, biomedical, robotic, infrastructure, and environmental applications. Their responses are shaped by nonlinear transduction, cross-sensitivity, conformal contact, manufacturing variation, drift, and limited calibration coverage. This review examines how machine learning (ML) can be used across the fiber-sensing pipeline, from algorithm-assisted physical design and fabrication-aware optimization to denoising, demodulation, representation learning, multimodal inference, and application-level decision making. Direct demonstrations in optical and electrically functional fiber systems are distinguished from transferable methods developed in adjacent photonic, additive manufacturing, tactile, and soft-sensor platforms. The available evidence is strong for calibration, signal recovery, and task inference within a defined device and operating domain. By contrast, experimental evidence for ML-guided physical co-design, cross-device and cross-batch transfer, long-term stability, and hardware-constrained deployment remains limited. Accordingly, ML is most promising as part of a coupled sensor–model–hardware system that preserves task-relevant information and reports when an input lies outside its validated operating range. This review therefore emphasizes validation boundaries over headline accuracy alone and identifies uncertainty quantification, physics-guided learning, fabrication metadata, and edge-aware co-design as priorities.

papers.abstract: Abstract The ILThermo database, the most comprehensive public collection of ionic liquid (IL) thermophysical measurements, covers fewer than one percent of all possible cation–anion pairs, leaving the vast majority of the IL design space experimentally uncharacterized. We report a machine learning pipeline that simultaneously predicts eight physicochemical and biological properties of ILs: density, dynamic viscosity, surface tension, refractive index, melting point, thermal decomposition temperature, glass transition temperature, and cytotoxicity, directly from molecular structure, without requiring prior experimental measurements for the target compound. Working from 32,455 experimental observations across 4,796 unique cation–anion pairs drawn from the ILPE.db curated data set, we train and evaluate six model classes under a strict pair-level split designed to prevent leakage between training and test sets; our analysis shows a naive row-level split would contaminate 59.6% of test pairs. The sequence spans Ridge regression, Random Forest, two Multi-Task Learning (MTL) neural networks, and two LightGBM variants using Morgan fingerprints or ChemBERTa embeddings as molecular representations. An R2-weighted ensemble of the four best-performing models achieves a mean test R2 of 0.752 across all eight properties (0.951 for density; 0.933 for refractive index). The ensemble is then used to screen 80,000 virtual IL pairs from the ILPE.db virtual library by combined model-disagreement uncertainty and Tanimoto novelty scoring, producing a prioritised experimental schedule that separates into uncertainty-driven and novelty-driven candidate clusters.

papers.title: Efficient stochastic fracture assessment of three-dimensional concrete structures: a machine learning-integrated phase field framework
papers.abstract: Fracture is one of the dominant deterioration and failure mechanisms affecting the serviceability and safety of concrete infrastructure. In practice, unavoidable variations in material properties and geometric configurations introduce significant uncertainties into fracture-governed structural responses, leading to substantial variability in structural performance and failure risk. Reliable assessment of such responses under uncertainty is essential for performance-based design and risk-informed asset management. However, the inherent complexity of fracture behaviour and the high computational demand of uncertainty quantification make such assessments particularly challenging. To address this challenge, this study proposes a phase field-based framework for stochastic assessment of fracture-governed structural responses in three-dimensional (3D) concrete structures. The framework combines a phase field model with an extended support vector regression (X-SVR) algorithm to establish mappings between uncertain inputs and targeted structural responses. To further improve predictive capability, a novel automatic relevance determination-generalised Hermite kernel (ARD-GHK) is developed and embedded into the X-SVR formulation. The resulting surrogate models enable rapid uncertainty quantification and statistical characterisation of fracture-governed structural responses over large ensembles of random realisations. Three representative 3D examples are employed to validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that the framework achieves excellent agreement with benchmark Monte Carlo simulations while reducing computational cost by several orders of magnitude. The proposed ARD-GHK is also shown to outperform polynomial and Gaussian kernels in surrogate modelling. By integrating high-fidelity fracture simulation with data-driven surrogate modelling, the framework provides an efficient computational approach for uncertainty quantification and structural safety evaluation of concrete infrastructure.

papers.title: Characteristics of carbon emissions during the construction phase of the Pinglu Canal
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s dual-carbon strategy, quantifying and characterizing carbon emissions during the construction phase of large-scale waterway infrastructure is critical for supporting the development of low-carbon transportation. This study takes the Pinglu Canal Project, a major inland waterway engineering project in China, as a case study. A carbon emission accounting framework based on the emission factor approach is developed to quantify construction-phase emissions. Spatiotemporal evolution patterns, sectoral differences, and emission intensity characteristics are systematically analyzed. Furthermore, data quality assessment using the Data Quality Indicator (DQI) method and uncertainty quantification based on Monte Carlo simulation are conducted to evaluate the robustness of the results. Results indicate that construction-phase carbon emissions exhibit a distinct stage-dependent pattern closely aligned with construction progress. By the first quarter of 2026, the cumulative emissions reached 9.26 million tonnes of CO 2 equivalent (tCO 2 e). Significant spatial heterogeneity is observed between engineering types, with hub structures contributing substantially higher emissions than waterway works due to differences in construction processes and material intensity. The overall carbon intensity of investment is estimated at 3.38 tCO 2 e per 10,000 CNY, representing a 16.75% reduction compared with typical hydropower infrastructure, indicating relatively low-carbon performance. Uncertainty analysis shows that material consumption, particularly concrete and steel usage, is the dominant source of variability in emission estimates, contributing over 80% of total uncertainty. The Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrate that the model outputs are statistically robust and consistent with deterministic calculations. This study establishes a comprehensive carbon accounting and uncertainty analysis framework for ultra-long linear waterway projects, providing methodological support for low-carbon design and management of similar large-scale infrastructure.

papers.title: A scenario-based stochastic MPC framework for coordinated HVAC and battery control in residential buildings
papers.abstract: Maintaining thermal comfort while reducing residential energy costs is challenging under uncertain weather conditions and increasing renewable energy penetration. This paper proposes a scenario-based stochastic Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for the coordinated operation of HVAC systems and battery energy storage. A validated 2R2C thermal model is integrated into the optimization process and calibrated using EnergyPlus simulations and measured residential data. Forecast uncertainty in ambient temperature and solar irradiance is represented through Monte Carlo scenario generation and scenario reduction. The controller minimizes electricity costs while enforcing thermal comfort constraints derived from ASHRAE Standard 55. Performance is evaluated across five Mediterranean climates using benchmark comparisons, ablation studies, robustness testing, and uncertainty quantification. Results show annual electricity cost reductions of 14–20% compared with conventional control strategies while maintaining comfort violations below 2%. Additional analyses demonstrate robust performance under extreme weather conditions and confirm the effectiveness of combining stochastic optimization, thermal modeling, and battery storage for residential energy flexibility. Practical Application This study provides building engineers and energy managers with a practical framework for coordinating residential HVAC systems, photovoltaic generation, and battery storage under uncertain weather conditions. Across five Mediterranean climates, the proposed controller achieves 14–20% annual electricity cost savings compared with conventional control, while keeping thermal comfort violations below 2%. Its reduced-order thermal model and scenario reduction approach support computationally efficient implementation in residential energy management systems. Practical deployment requires building-specific calibration, periodic forecast updates, and appropriate fallback controls to maintain safe and reliable operation.

papers.title: Bio-electrochemical swarm intelligence with quantum constrained graph learning for distributed battery optimization in urban microgrids
papers.abstract: The integration of distributed battery storage in urban microgrids is becoming increasingly common. Yet, most existing methods for optimizing urban microgrid operation are incapable of jointly representing battery physics, device-to-device relationships, and the temporal variability of intermittent renewable generation. Conventional swarm and deterministic methods also commonly rely on random initialization, homogeneous agent behavior, or post-hoc constraint handling. Therefore, this research proposes a unifying framework that integrates five key components into a single pipeline: (1) Bio-Electrochemical Swarm Field Initialization (BESFI); (2) Adaptive Multi-Species Co-Evolutionary Swarm Routing (AMSCESR); (3) a Spatio-Temporal Energy Diffusion Graph Transformer (STED-GT); (4) Quantum-Inspired Stability-Constrained Optimization (QISCO); and (5) a Digital Twin Reinforcement Validation Engine (DT-RVE). The novelty lies in the closed coupling of physics-aware initialization, role-diverse swarm search, relational graph learning, in-loop stability filtering, and digital-twin reinforcement validation rather than in any isolated module. On the reported 25-node urban microgrid testbed, the framework achieved 95.8% dispatch accuracy, 94.6% energy efficiency, ± 3.7% voltage deviation, ± 0.019 Hz frequency deviation, 10.6% capacity fade, and 2.3 s supervisory adaptation latency. These results indicate improved load balancing, grid stability, battery-life preservation, and adaptive operation within the evaluated simulation conditions.

papers.title: A TCN-KANformer-MDN model for engine remaining useful life prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life of aircraft engines is critical to the safety of aircraft operations. Targeting the two problems of modeling complex nonlinear degradation relationships and quantifying prediction uncertainty, this paper proposes a novel RUL prediction model that integrates a temporal convolutional network (TCN), KANformer, and a mixture density network (MDN). In the proposed framework, the TCN is first employed to extract multi-scale temporal dependency features from the degradation sequences. Subsequently, the KANformer is introduced to perform nonlinear transformations on the extracted features, leveraging its learnable basis functions to enhance the model’s capacity for characterizing complex degradation patterns. Finally, the MDN outputs a probability density distribution of the RUL, thereby enabling quantitative uncertainty quantification of the predictions. Experimental validation on the NASA C-MAPSS dataset demonstrates that, in comparison with benchmark methods such as Cau-DA-LSTM, the proposed TCN-KANformer-MDN model achieves approximately 10% improvement in both prediction accuracy and uncertainty quantification metrics, fully corroborating its effectiveness and robustness under complex operating conditions.

papers.title: Hierarchical Cloud-Edge Cooperative Control Framework for Multi-Vehicle Autonomous Driving Using Reinforcement Learning and Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: This study presents a hierarchical cooperative control framework for hybrid electric vehicles in intelligent transportation systems, termed “cloud-coordinated cooperative driving with deep reinforcement learning.” The framework integrates reinforcement learning with model predictive control (MPC) to balance adaptability and stability. A cloud-level coordinator utilizes the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm for global policy optimization, while each vehicle executes a local Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) controller for real-time adaptive control. A predecessor–leader–follower-based cooperative economic MPC module is incorporated to ensure stable spacing and energy-efficient trajectory tracking. Furthermore, a hybrid offline–online learning mechanism with state synchronization and experience replay enhances convergence speed and generalization capability. Under three representative driving cycles: highway fuel economy test, US06 (a high-speed, high-acceleration cycle), and China light-duty vehicle test cycle with an initial state-of-charge (SOC) of 0.60, the proposed MADDPG-SAC algorithm consistently outperforms deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) and MADDPG. This method attains lower fuel consumption (17.93–20.62 L/100 km), higher minimum SOC (0.33–0.35), reduced speed tracking error (0.22–0.26 m/s) and spacing error (0.29–0.35 m), smoother control (mean jerk of 0.041–0.049 m/s 3 ), and faster convergence (11–13 episodes compared with 12–29 episodes for DDPG and MADDPG). Overall, the framework exhibits strong cooperative capability, energy efficiency, and driving stability, demonstrating its potential for large-scale energy-aware autonomous driving applications.

papers.abstract: Abstract Predicting the ammonium nitrogen (NH4+-N) adsorption capacity of biochar is challenged by coupled, nonlinear interactions among operational variables, pyrolysis synthesis parameters, and intrinsic material properties. A unified data set comprising 425 literature-reported adsorption records from 18 studies was compiled, and preprocessing (KNN imputation and Z-score standardization) was fitted exclusively on the training subset to prevent data leakage. Among seven machine learning algorithms benchmarked with Bayesian optimization and 5-fold cross-validation, XGBoost achieved the highest test-set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.901 and root-mean-square error of 0.555 mg g–1. TreeSHAP analysis quantitatively decoupled three driver groups, adsorption operational parameters (53.3%), biochar physicochemical properties (38.2%), and pyrolysis synthesis parameters (8.5%), and identified initial concentration, biochar oxygen content, and adsorbent dosage as the dominant variables, with oxygen content exhibiting a unimodal relationship with adsorption capacity. Partial dependence plots were further utilized to reveal nonlinear response behaviors and determine data-coverage-validated optimal operation and design windows for key variables. A graphical user interface was developed to estimate equilibrium adsorption capacity, reducing reliance on extensive laboratory trials.

papers.title: A two-branch physics-informed neural network for small-sample sedimentation prediction of magnetorheological fluids
papers.abstract: Abstract Sedimentation tests of magnetorheological fluids (MRFs) under natural gravity are time-consuming, limiting the experimental coverage of particle concentrations and formulations. This study proposes a moving-boundary data-interpolated physics-informed network (MB-DIP) to jointly predict concentration-field evolution and mudline motion from a limited number of measured source samples and the known initial state of a target sample. The two-branch architecture combines a physical mudline prior with a moving-boundary-aligned concentration-field prior. Conservation-constrained field refinement and reliability-guided interface consistency refinement subsequently coordinate local particle transport, overall particle content, and interface motion. For baseline MRFs, samples with initial particle volume fractions of 7.5, 10, 15, and 32 vol% were used to predict sedimentation at 20 and 26 vol%. The mean absolute errors of the concentration field and mudline position were 2.04% and 1.96 mm, respectively, and the mean absolute percentage error of particle content was 2.83%. Ablation experiments demonstrated the contribution of physics-consistency refinement, while six-fold leave-one-source-concentration-out validation examined prediction performance under varying source-data coverage. Further validation used SiO₂-modified MRFs containing 28 vol% carbonyl iron particles and 0.25–1 wt% silica. MB-DIP captured changes in sedimentation behavior with silica content, whereas the theoretical predictions remained unchanged. Concentration-field and mudline mean absolute errors ranged from 0.620% to 1.872% and from 0.306 to 1.081 mm, respectively. These results support MB-DIP as a method for predicting MRF sedimentation under limited-data conditions, with potential to reduce the experimental effort required for formulation evaluation.

Accurate current estimation is essential for high-performance brushless DC (BLDC) motor drives, especially in finite control set model predictive control (FCSMPC), where prediction accuracy directly affects control quality. Problem. Sliding mode observers (SMOs) are widely adopted for this purpose due to their robustness against modeling uncertainties. However, the performance of conventional SMO strongly depends on proper gain tuning, which is typically fixed and may lead to degraded performance under parameter variations and changing operating conditions. Goal. To develop an adaptive SMO gain strategy that automatically adjusts the observer gain online using recursive least squares (RLS) approach to improve robustness and estimation accuracy of the ultra local model without manual tuning. Methodology. The proposed method proposes the SMO gain adaptation as an online regression problem, where the RLS algorithm is used to recursively update the observer gain at each sampling instant. The adaptive SMO is integrated into an FCSMPC scheme. Its performance is evaluated through simulations under nominal conditions and parameter mismatches and compared with static-gain and PI-based adaptive SMO approaches using dynamic and steady-state performance metrics. Results. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RLS-based adaptive gain SMO achieves faster convergence, reduced chattering, and improved robustness against parameter variations. Scientific novelty. The main contribution of this work is the use of RLS to adapt the SMO gain rather than directly estimating system parameters, providing a stable and statistically grounded gain adaptation mechanism. Practical value. The method reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of the sliding variable by 5.8 % compared to the static-gain approach and provides faster settling time and lower steady-state error in speed response. The settling time is reduced by 33 % and decreasing steady-state error by 58 % compared to the conventional static-gain approach. In addition, the adaptive mechanism enhances robustness under parameter mismatch and load disturbance conditions. References 34, tables 3, figures 6.

papers.title: Explainable Machine Learning for Next-Hour Prediction Using Three Meteorological Variables and Historical PM2.5 Data
papers.abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remains one of the most consequential urban air-quality hazards, yet forecasting its next-hour concentration accurately and transparently remains challenging owing to the non-linear, multivariate nature of pollutant-meteorology interactions and the black-box character of high-performing ensemble models. This study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for next-hour PM2.5 concentration prediction that integrates Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with a parsimonious set of predictors comprising three meteorological variables (air temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed) together with historical PM2.5 concentrations. Using 43,824 hourly observations from the Beijing PM2.5 dataset (2010–2014), lag, rolling-statistic, and cyclical calendar features were engineered, and model hyperparameters were systematically tuned through Bayesian optimization using the Optuna framework with the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator over 30 trials under a strictly chronological training validation testing split. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. The tuned XGBoost model achieved a root mean squared error of 16.50 µg/m³, a mean absolute error of 9.89 µg/m³, a mean absolute percentage error of 21.75%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.9478 on the test set, corresponding to reductions of approximately 4.4%, 10.5%, and 12.4% in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, respectively, relative to a non-optimized baseline model. SHAP analysis revealed that the one-hour PM2.5 lag feature overwhelmingly dominated the model's predictions, far surpassing the combined contribution of all meteorological variables, while wind speed and temperature retained secondary but physically meaningful influence. These findings demonstrate that a minimal, readily obtainable feature set can support highly accurate and interpretable next-hour PM2.5 forecasting, offering a practical and scientifically transparent tool to support early-warning air-quality systems and evidence-based environmental health policy.

papers.title: Methods for efficient eutectic screening in CALPHAD databases
papers.abstract: Eutectic points play a critical role in material science due to their low melting points, absence of a solidification range, and formation of unique microstructures that enhance properties. However, identifying eutectics in calculated ternary and higher-order systems remains computationally challenging due to the lack of a well-established screening approach. This work addresses this gap by developing a general, efficient methodology for efficient eutectic screening in multicomponent systems. We first propose and benchmark four CALPHAD-based methods for eutectic identification, evaluating their computational speed and reliability. We then investigate the potential of combining CALPHAD with machine learning to further accelerate the process, leveraging two eutectic properties: (1) eutectics are local minima on the liquidus, and (2) they lie at the intersections of primary crystallization regions. Active learning surrogate models are employed to interpolate CALPHAD data for predicting liquidus and primary crystallization phases, and the performance of each approach is evaluated. By benchmarking multiple strategies and releasing code for three approaches that enable rapid and reliable eutectic screening in high-order systems, this work advances the design of materials such as cast alloys, phase change materials, eutectic high entropy alloys, or metallic glasses.

papers.title: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials
papers.abstract: Recent work has improved computer-use agents (CUAs) by combining retrieved task-relevant tutorials and look-ahead planning using world models with MLLM judges. However, the contribution of each component -- tutorials, the judge, and the world model -- to overall improvement has not been evaluated in isolation. To fill this gap, we first construct OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial: two datasets for CUAs with curated multimodal tutorials, covering everyday and scientific domains. We then propose RAG-PolicyJudge (RAG-PJ), a policy-judge framework for CUAs conditioned on task-specific tutorials: the policy proposes candidate actions, and the judge selects among them. To isolate the effect of world models given tutorials, we compare RAG-PJ with and without common world models: using either zero-shot text-based descriptions of next states or an oracle that returns ground-truth visual observations. We find that RAG-PJ gains little benefit from these rollouts when tutorials are present, even with perfect visual futures. This suggests prior world-model gains in tutorial-conditioned methods come mainly from tutorial understanding and the judge's ability to select the proposed actions, rather than from predicted rollouts. Error analysis reveals that the bottleneck is not rollout fidelity, but the judge's ability to reason over future states and recognize task completion. This highlights the need to improve not just next-state prediction in world models, but also reasoning over their predicted rollouts. Datasets and code are available at https://github.com/realjoenguyen/RAGPJ-official.

papers.title: Graph-Localized Coverage for Conformal Prediction on Inductive Graphs
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) provides marginal coverage guarantees, but marginal coverage does not determine where prediction errors occur on a graph. Queries from different graph neighborhoods can exhibit substantially different levels of uncertainty even when aggregate coverage remains near its target. We introduce GLocalCP, an online CP framework for inductive node classification and edge prediction that combines marginal and graph-local calibration with uncertainty-adaptive prediction sets. Specifically, GLocalCP puts forth a novel uncertainty-adaptive nonconformality score that relies on the mutual information obtained from Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout based prediction. Then, it augments a global online threshold with a kernel-based local correction that propagates coverage feedback among similar graph queries. On the theoretical horizon, we establish pathwise $O(N^{-1/2})$ marginal calibration error without exchangeability or stationarity and, for the exact-kernel formulation, an explicit $O(N^{-1/2})$ graph-localized calibration guarantee. Experiments on seven node-classification and seven edge-prediction benchmarks show that similar marginal coverage can conceal substantially different local reliability. Our proposed GLocalCP maintains coverage near the target while consistently reducing graph-local calibration error. Uncertainty scaling in GLocalCP further reduces prediction-set size across all evaluated node and edge datasets while leaving marginal coverage essentially unchanged.

We showcase the flexibility of this approach by demonstrating significant improvements across a range of tasks, including Bayesian optimization, model-based reinforcement learning, and transductive learning.

papers.abstract: Effective world modeling requires compressing salient history information that facilitates future prediction. Compression Forcing features Dynamics-Aware Tokenization (DAT), a novel tokenization method that compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. Built on a diffusion backbone, this structure enables Hierarchical History Guidance (HG-H), allowing selective amplification of dynamics-salient information during inference. Extensive experiments across various environments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making performance, establishing Compression Forcing as a highly flexible and effective approach for world modeling.

papers.title: Physical Experience Builds Continual Spatial World Models
papers.abstract: World models are increasingly used to support prediction and planning in embodied agents, but the knowledge is usually established before deployment and then carried into later encounters. A physics-grounded dynamic maze separates recurring spatial change from the continuous consequences of action. Cross-episode Spatial Change Memory learns relations among environmental transformations, while state-action-outcome experience refines predictions of motion. Structured experience progressively reduces the need for future route correction and transfers to spatial transitions not encountered during learning. The advantage disappears when past changes contain no information about future ones. Continuous navigation further shows that predictive memory changes behavior when a previous decision becomes invalid but leaves behavior unchanged when the decision remains correct. Physical tests expose a complementary limit: correct topology does not guarantee correct action prediction, and accumulated physical experience reduces this mismatch within the modeled dynamics. The results characterize continual world knowledge as experience that improves future prediction and action beyond stored episodes while remaining revisable by the physical outcomes it is intended to predict.

papers.abstract: To enable effective generalization in offline meta-RL, it is essential to accurately infer the underlying task through latent task representations, which provide a compact and transferable summary of task-specific characteristics for guiding policy generation. The learned task representations are used as conditioning signals for a DT-based policy, enabling task-aware meta-policy learning. To further support generalization in both zero-shot and few-shot settings, we design a language-grounded, self-adaptive strategy that enables effective and reliable adaptation to unseen tasks. Notably, in CoTA-DT, the pretrained LLM serves as a shared backbone for language encoding, world modeling, Q-function estimation, and policy learning. This unified design facilitates parameter sharing, improving both efficiency and generalization. Extensive experiments across diverse offline meta-RL benchmarks demonstrate that CoTA-DT consistently outperforms prior methods, particularly in challenging zero-shot generalization scenarios.

papers.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients force a neural solver to spend capacity on a scale that the equation already determines. We show that a single classical object, the Ermakov-Pinney scale function $ρ$, can be written into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free embedding. One construction covers three problem families through the two signs of the Pinney constant $c$: linear diffusion ($c=-1$, $ω\equiv0$), diffusion in a time-dependent confining trap ($c=-1$, $ω\neq0$), and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency ($c=+1$). An exact moment identity gives $ρ$ in closed form from the initial data alone, so no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution is needed. Our central finding is comparative: each family requires a different component of the construction and has a different honest control. In family I, the diffusive-time reparametrisation alone reproduces most of the gain, so that family is a poor test of the idea and shows why an ablation is mandatory. In family II no time reparametrisation exists, the control degrades accuracy, and the amplitude prefactor becomes essential (40.8x). In family III the adiabatic approximation also fails, and the quadratic phase factor is what matters (5.7x). The method does not help when the reduced solution does not converge to a fixed point: its extrapolation advantage then disappears. The reduction itself is the classical scaling-variable change of the self-similar-asymptotics literature; what is new is the moment identity that makes it architectural for time-dependent coefficients, and the comparative anatomy above.

papers.abstract: Koopman representations describe nonlinear dynamics through linear evolution in a transformed space, offering an attractive framework for their linear simplicity and generality. Yet these advantages do not necessarily translate into improved performance in deep latent data assimilation (LDA). We systematically compare seven representative methods and structural baselines across five systems spanning approximately periodic to strongly chaotic dynamics and a broad range of state dimensions. We evaluate forecast and assimilation accuracy, physical state recovery, latent-trajectory behavior, and dynamical consistency, and assess Gaussian error assumptions, objective convexity, and uniqueness of analysis solutions. Our results reveal a trade-off between representational flexibility and optimization tractability. Linear evolution of the latent state can stabilize short-term forecasts but restrict expressiveness in strongly chaotic and high-dimensional systems, without consistently improving assimilation accuracy. Parameterized linear operators offer greater flexibility, yet their joint optimization with the encoder--decoder remains nonconvex. Methods with closed-form analysis updates generally perform better and exhibit greater robustness in our experiments, although matrix inversion remains a computational bottleneck. These findings show that the practical benefits of Koopman structure depend on both sufficient observational information and the choice of assimilation procedure.

papers.abstract: Score-learning methods generally lack pointwise supervision, which affects the training accuracy, particularly in regions where SDE trajectories are rare. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel method called \emph{BEL anchors}, which uses Monte Carlo score estimates at user-selected space-time query points. By combining a Feynman--Kac representation of the Fokker--Planck equation with the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula, our estimator requires neither closed-form transition densities, spatial discretization, nor derivatives of the initial density. We derive its asymptotic variance and use the anchors as sparse supervised targets for existing score-learning objectives. Experiments show that BEL anchors improve implicit score matching in poorly sampled regions, prevent score-PINN collapse, and enable accurate sample regeneration in several numerical examples.

papers.title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale
papers.abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) returns a single optimal configuration, systematically discarding the explored performance landscape that encodes how results depend on configuration choices. Fitness landscape analysis comprises a robust collection of methods from evolutionary computation offering ruggedness indices, autocorrelation functions, and fitness-distance correlation that have never been applied to machine learning hyperparameter spaces at scale, given that fine-grained ground-truth enumeration data has not existed. We present ExaTune, an open-source HPC system to produce a new artifact class: the hyperparameter landscape map. ExaTune exhaustively evaluates every point on a discretized hyperparameter grid via $K$-fold cross-validation, aggregates results into reproducible parquet benchmarks, and applies a suite of five formalized landscape metrics: spatial autocorrelation (Moran's $I$), ruggedness, local optima density, fitness-distance correlation (FDC), and variance-based parameter importance. We release a benchmark collection of 8 complete landscape maps (totalling 285,080 exhaustively evaluated configurations) spanning five model families (SVMs, random forests, XGBoost, ridge regression, and $k$-nearest neighbors) across six classification and two regression benchmarks, hosted on HuggingFace. Empirical analysis demonstrates that Bayesian optimization, Optuna, Hyperband, and Random Search at standard trial budgets systematically miss instability regions, secondary optima, and parameter interaction effects that are visible in complete landscapes; information that is structurally unavailable to any optimizer by design.

papers.title: Topology‐Dependent Sequential Crushing and Energy Absorption in Axially Hybridized TPMS Lattices
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Axial hybridization provides a means of tailoring the crushing response of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices. FRD lattices exhibit high resistance after yielding and strong energy absorption, motivating their use in hybrid designs. However, how the topology paired with FRD influences regional deformation and energy absorption remains unclear. In this study, G, P, and IWP were paired with FRD using the same axial arrangement, sigmoid transition, dimensions and target global relative density. Quasistatic compression tests on poly(lactic acid) lattices fabricated by fused deposition modeling provided mechanical and energy absorption metrics, while finite element simulations aided interpretation of regional deformation. For the homogeneous lattices, resistance after yielding decreased in the order FRD, IWP, G, and P. In G–FRD, however, the FRD region deformed first. G–FRD maintained relatively continuous resistance but densified earlier than P–FRD, which recovered resistance after an initial load drop. Among the hybrids, IWP–FRD exhibited two distinct stages of load bearing, with the lowest initial peak stress of 3.00 MPa, the highest mean plateau stress of 5.25 MPa, and the highest specific energy absorption of 13.36 J/g. Base topology thus influences regional deformation and compaction, shaping the crushing response and energy absorption.

Patients with GLL (Beighton ⩾4) were matched 1:2 to controls (Beighton ⩽3) by age, sex, BMI, and follow-up. Outcomes included PROMs changes, achievement of MCID/PASS, complications, and revisions. RESULTS: > 0.05): 1 GLL patient (2.4%) for infection and 1 control (1.2%) for aseptic loosening. No dislocations occurred. papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Selection of 3D Printing Parameters for Hybrid Biomaterial Scaffolds: A Leakage-Controlled, Multi-Objective Analysis of Open Bioprinting and Fused Deposition Data
papers.abstract: Hybrid tissue-engineering scaffolds combine a printed thermoplastic frame for load bearing with a cell-laden hydrogel for biological function, but their printing parameters are usually chosen by trial and error. This study evaluates whether open data and machine learning can guide that choice. Three openly released datasets were used: 617 extrusion-bioprinting cell-viability records and 339 filament-printability records compiled from 75 published studies, and 500 fused deposition modelling runs with tensile and surface measurements. Each dataset was modelled separately with ridge or logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, Gaussian process and multilayer perceptron models under repeated nested cross-validation. Splits for the bioprinting data were grouped by source study to prevent leakage. Models were interpreted with SHAP values and partial dependence, and NSGA-II and exhaustive surrogate search with bootstrap uncertainty and an applicability-domain constraint were used to propose parameter windows. Tensile strength and modulus were predicted accurately (XGBoost R² = 0.92 and 0.96). Printability transferred moderately to unseen studies (AUC = 0.82), whereas continuous viability did not (best R² = 0.01). Random K-fold splitting inflated viability R² from -0.27 to 0.49 and printability AUC from 0.63 to 0.96. PLA+ frame settings with predicted lower-bound strength above 30 MPa were found at up to 80 % nominal void fraction. No alginate-based bioink window inside the data domain met both the viability and printability targets with confidence. Literature-pooled bioprinting data therefore support frame design but not quantitative bioink design across laboratories, and all recommendations require experimental validation.

papers.title: Recursive Inference for Heterogeneous Multi-Output Gaussian Process State-Space Models
papers.abstract: Accurate learning of system dynamics is becoming increasingly crucial for advanced control and decision-making in engineering. However, real-world systems often exhibit multiple channels and highly nonlinear transition dynamics, challenging traditional modeling methods. To enable online learning for these systems, this paper formulates the system as Gaussian process state-space models (GPSSMs) and develops a recursive learning method. The main contributions are threefold. First, a heterogeneous multi-output kernel is designed, allowing each output dimension to adopt distinct kernel types, hyperparameters, and input variables, improving expressiveness in multidimensional dynamics learning. Second, an inducing-point management algorithm enhances computational efficiency through independent selection and pruning for each output dimension. Third, a unified recursive inference framework for GPSSMs is derived, supporting general moment-matching approaches, including the extended Kalman filter, unscented Kalman filter, and assumed density filtering, enabling accurate learning under strong nonlinearity and significant noise. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that the proposed method matches the accuracy of state-of-the-art (SOTA) offline GPSSMs with only 1/100 of the runtime and surpasses SOTA online GPSSMs by around 70% in accuracy under heavy noise while using only 1/20 of the runtime.

papers.title: BIM–digital twin integration for construction safety: Mechanisms, maturity pathways, and socio-technical progression
papers.abstract: The construction industry continues to experience high rates of serious injury and fatality worldwide, motivating an increasing interest in advanced digitalization strategies that combine building information modeling (BIM) with digital twin (DT) capabilities. By linking static semantic site models with continuous field data, these systems offer a powerful approach to proactive risk management. However, while individual remote sensing and predictive analytics components are well researched, a unified understanding of how these BIM and DT safety systems are integrated remains critically limited. Specifically, there is a clear need to understand how system capabilities evolve across different maturity stages and what underlying factors drive this progression across the construction lifecycle. This paper presents a comprehensive scoping review of BIM and DT integration for construction safety management across the entire project lifecycle. Using a tiered evidence strategy and structured thematic coding, the existing literature is synthesized through three main analytical lenses: integration mechanisms and data exchange patterns, maturity characteristics and capability horizons, and the socio-technical factors that systematically influence maturity transitions. This review clarifies the dominant architectural integration approaches and maps current proof-of-concept efforts against the requirements for more predictive and governance-ready safety twins. The findings indicate that most implementations remain at the interactive monitoring stage, with predictive capability emerging mainly in data-rich contexts and autonomous adaptation not yet realized. Furthermore, it identifies persistent bottlenecks in data interoperability and real-time processing that currently hinder widespread industry adoption. Finally, the study proposes a focused research agenda designed to help transition these intelligent monitoring systems from isolated prototypes to robust, scalable applications suitable for safety-critical construction environments.

papers.title: Empirical and physics-based computational approaches to explosive power, brisance, and underwater detonation response: A critical review with selected machine-learning applications
papers.abstract: Reliable interpretation of energetic-material performance requires methods that connect thermochemical properties and detonation behavior with clearly defined experimental endpoints. This critical narrative review examines empirical correlations, thermochemical calculations, numerical models, and selected machine-learning (ML) applications relevant to three domains: explosive power, brisance, and underwater detonation response. The principal emphasis is on established empirical and physics-based computational approaches used to estimate intrinsic detonation properties or interpret test-derived performance measures. Empirical correlations are transparent and computationally efficient, but their reliability depends on the data and conditions for which they were developed. Thermochemical and numerical models represent physical processes more explicitly, although their predictions remain sensitive to input data, model assumptions, and boundary conditions. ML studies are included where they directly inform the reviewed domains, including QSPR/read-across estimation of thermochemical properties, prediction of density and detonation descriptors, and surrogate modeling of underwater fluid or structural response. These studies address different targets and use labels derived from experiments, empirical equations, or numerical simulations; consequently, their reported error metrics are not directly comparable. Representative methods are compared in terms of prediction target, required inputs, assumptions, validation evidence, computational burden, and limitations. The review is not intended as a comprehensive survey of ML architectures or general-purpose energetic-material discovery, because the available evidence is uneven across the three performance domains. Instead, it identifies where empirical, physics-based, and data-driven methods can complement one another and where further validation is needed. A proposed integration strategy is outlined that combines empirical baselines, thermochemical or numerical calculations, ML surrogates, physics-informed constraints where governing equations are available, active learning, and calibrated uncertainty estimates. This strategy is presented as a research direction rather than an independently validated framework spanning all three domains.

papers.title: From maxwell to digital twins: a physics-based framework for future AI-native wireless communications
papers.abstract: Wireless digital twins are emerging as a critical technology for next-generation communications. Constructing these twins is challenging because it requires modeling not only environmental geometry, but also complex electromagnetic (EM) properties and interactions. Rooted in classical EM theory, our study shows that accurate wireless digital twin construction depends on properly representing and learning essential intrinsic scene parameters–geometry, material properties, and propagation mechanisms–embedded in the PDE structure of Maxwell’s equations. We propose a neural methodology that leverages deep learning to learn the underlying physics directly from data, achieving high-quality reconstruction and robust generalization across changing environments. papers.abstract: High benchmark accuracy does not inform a security operations center which alerts to trust or whether attacks absent from training can be flagged. Primary analyses use the first-occurrence feature deduplication. Novelty performance was family dependent and sometimes inverted: four families had probability-space area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of at least 0.70, while the nearest-neighbor AUROC was at most 0.45, including web attacks (0.966 vs. 0.298), whereas port scanning reversed the ordering (0.166 vs. 0.812). The benign-only isolation forest was weaker overall; a matched forest fitted on all known classes also remained family dependent. Marginal conformal coverage was near 0.900, whereas one class fell to 0.295. Class-conditional calibration raised every seed-averaged class coverage to at least 0.894, including the class with 35 calibration examples. Its efficiency depended strongly on the base classifier: Rule B auto-dispatch was 0.3% for gradient boosting on UNSW-NB15 but 70.4% for a random forest. Calibration-selected probability thresholds often achieve similar or lower selective risk, whereas among the methods compared, only the conformal constructions supplied finite-sample coverage control. The conformal correction modestly improved the worst-class coverage over a per-class empirical quantile using the same order-statistic convention. These results position conformal prediction as a coverage control mechanism rather than a universal novelty detector or automation advantage.

papers.title: Optimal control of financial inclusion for women entrepreneurs with bifurcation, statistical and stochastic analysis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a comprehensive mathematical model incorporating market linkages, sociocultural interventions, social capital, and access to finance to examine the dynamics of women entrepreneurs. We extend the deterministic model by incorporating the random variations present in socioeconomic systems, in addition to constructiing and analyzing a stochastic nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) scheme. The methodology overcomes significant limitations of traditional numerical approaches by ensuring the preservation of positivity and boundedness for all step sizes. We compute key thresholds at which the system undergoes qualitative behavioral changes by using eigenvalue analysis, one-dimensional parameter sweeps, and two-dimensional stability surfaces. The absence of flip bifurcation verifies that the behaviour of the system is bounded and that the system does not exhibit period-doubling instabilities. The stochastic and deterministic simulations highlight the dynamic behavior of the suggested model. The impact of parameters, illustrated through radial, tornado, chord, and heat-map diagrams, shows that maintenance programs that lower the depreciation rate through regulatory change should be combined with initiatives that improve investment rates through financial literacy and digital infrastructure. Statistical validation shows the superiority of the nonstandard finite difference scheme and the effectiveness of control measures compared with the no-control case. By formulating a stochastic optimal control problem, we compare four policy cases with the no-control case, and the results show that the combination of all controls produces the highest access to finance. The NSFD scheme preserves positivity for all step sizes, whereas Euler-Maruyama generates economically non-feasible negative results for large step sizes. The findings indicate that, to prevent irregular losses in entrepreneurial capacity, effective interventions should prioritize stabilizing social networks and controlling financial access during turbulent periods, which underscores the importance of stable policy environments and consistent financial support mechanisms. In women's entrepreneurial development programs, our study offers a strong foundation for policy modeling, uncertainty quantification, and evidence-based decision-making.

papers.title: Fatigue Life Prediction of Ultrahigh Performance Concrete Using Gaussian Process Regression With SHAP Interpretation and Yeo–Johnson Transformation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of the fatigue life of ultrahigh performance concrete (UHPC), due to its complex multiparameter dependent nonlinear behavior, presents a major challenge for ensuring structural safety and durability. To address this issue, this study integrates machine learning algorithms with interpretability analysis to develop a high‐precision prediction model. The Yeo–Johnson transformation was employed to correct the pronounced positive skewness of the UHPC fatigue life data. Through a systematic evaluation of seven machine learning algorithms, the hyperparameter‐optimized Gaussian Process Regression model exhibited the best overall performance ( R 2 = 0.9931, MAPE = 1.410%). Validation against the source data further confirmed the robustness of Gaussian process regression (GPR) with an R 2 of 0.939, significantly outperforming the existing model ( R 2 = 0.665). Furthermore, Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis revealed that coarse aggregate volume, cube compressive strength, and stress level are the dominant influencing factors, accounting for over 85% of the prediction variability. Consequently, this research provides a robust engineering framework for the assessment of UHPC fatigue life.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Modalities, Frameworks, and Clinical Tasks
papers.abstract: The diagnosis of colorectal cancer encompasses nine complementary modalities: stool-based screening, blood-based biomarkers, cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic evaluation, histopathology, liquid biopsy, molecular and genetic profiling, microbiome analysis, and nanotechnology-based diagnostics. This narrative review synthesizes 160 references spanning seven task-specific artificial intelligence domains, including computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology and radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, neoadjuvant treatment response prediction, and surgical workflow analysis. We propose a conceptual multimodal pipeline comprising data ingestion, preprocessing and harmonization, feature representation, multimodal fusion, forecasting, explainability, and validation. A structured evidence grading framework classifies each clinical task by evidence level, consistency, and clinical readiness. We further catalog public datasets, challenge benchmarks, and five reporting standards: TRIPOD-AI, CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and CLAIM. Computer-aided detection and optical diagnosis demonstrate the highest maturity with Level 1 evidence from randomized controlled trials, while computational pathology, radiogenomics, and metastasis prediction remain at Level 2 with retrospective validation (internal or external). Microbiome screening, nanotechnology diagnostics, and surgical phase recognition are exploratory. The principal barriers to clinical adoption are domain shift, data scarcity, calibration, prospective validation, and workflow integration. We conclude that clinically useful artificial intelligence requires robust external validation, uncertainty quantification, explainable outputs, standardized reporting, and a structured translational pathway from retrospective evidence through regulatory clearance to post-deployment monitoring.

At 110 and 70 km/h with adhesion coefficients of 0.80 and 0.50, the increases are 58.0% and 158.2%. No overestimation is observed on the evaluation grid. In the first two conditions, peak sideslip-angle errors decrease by 36.4% and 45.2% relative to permissive fixed-boundary control, while peak additional yaw moments are 72.7% and 63.2% lower than with conservative fixed-boundary control. At 80 km/h with adhesion coefficient of 0.35, peak sideslip-angle error decreases by 55.8% relative to no yaw-moment control. papers.title: Surrogate Model for Rubber Spring and Damping Elements Based on High-fidelity Simulations of Cyclically Loaded Vulcanizates
papers.abstract: This paper presents a surrogate modeling approach for predicting the cyclic stiffness characteristics of rubber spring and damping elements (RSDE) used in vibration isolation systems. The methodology is based on high-fidelity finite element (FE) simulations that incorporate geometry-dependent assembly effects and advanced material modeling of filled vulcanizates subjected to cyclic loading. The constitutive framework combines the Modified Extended Tube Model (METM) with Advanced Mullins Damage Modeling (AMDM), providing a physically motivated description of hyperelasticity, stress softening, and steady-state hysteretic behavior. The resulting three-dimensional FE implementation was realized as an Abaqus user material subroutine and validated against experimental measurements of commercial RSDEs. Simulated torque-angle characteristics showed excellent agreement with experiments, with peak torque deviations below ±3%. To enable rapid engineering predictions, a parameterized FE model covering representative RSDE geometries was used to generate a design-of-experiments dataset. The simulated loading characteristics were condensed into three physically interpretable parameters describing cyclic stiffness behavior and subsequently approximated using multi-linear response surface regression models. The surrogate model links six geometric design variables to the non-linear torque-angle response, achieving high predictive accuracy with adjusted coefficients of determination R2adj up to 0.977. Analysis of the regression model reveals the influence of rubber cord dimensions and profile geometry on stiffness evolution under torsional loading. Comparison with independent test cases demonstrates that the surrogate model reliably reproduces FE predictions within the considered design space. The proposed surrogate model enables real-time estimation of geometry- and material-dependent cyclic stiffness characteristics, supporting efficient design and optimization of customized RSDE applications without testing.

papers.abstract: A finite element model of a Charnley® total hip prosthesis was developed based on 3D scanning and digital geometric repair to evaluate its biomechanical behavior during the critical phase of gait. Models with and without muscle forces were compared, incorporating biomaterial properties, implant–femur interaction, and acetabular backing using Abaqus® software. The results showed good agreement with the literature and demonstrated that the inclusion of abductor and gluteal muscles produces a more uniform stress distribution. Furthermore, the presence of stress shielding was identified in the proximal femoral region, associated with insufficient load transfer and potential bone resorption processes. The study demonstrates that considering muscle forces improves the biomechanical representation and the identification of critical regions related to wear and failure.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization of Surfactin Titer Produced by Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423 from Minimum Fermentation Data with Experimental Validation
papers.abstract: Abstract Optimizing surfactin production from a wild-type Bacillus sp., is challenging due to complex microbial growth kinetics, nonlinear interactions among process variables, and the lack of mechanistic models to describe surfactin production. Therefore, the present study develops data-driven machine learning models to optimize surfactin production from Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423 under limited fermentation data. First, 25 batch fermentation experiments were performed to obtain surfactin titers under varied conditions of temperature, agitation speed, and inoculum volume, generated using a central composite design (CCD) integrated with maximin Latin hypercube sampling (LHS). Subsequently, machine learning models, viz, multivariable least-squares regression (MVLSR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), support vector regression (SVR), and random forest (RF), were trained and evaluated using the nested leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to achieve robust prediction of the surfactin titer. Hyperparameter tuning of the models was performed using a genetic algorithm (GA) and grid search. Both the GPR and SVR outperformed the other models and demonstrated comparable predictive performance on the unseen data, producing the LOOCV R2 of 0.89 and 0.86, and LOOCV RMSE of 0.6 and 0.67, respectively. Subsequently, the mean response surface plots were constructed using the GPR model to illustrate the effects of nonlinear interactions among the input features on the surfactin titer. Finally, a GPR-based constrained optimization yielded an optimal surfactin titer of 5.72 g L–1, compared to the base-case value of 1.49 g L–1, while identifying the optimal process variables. The data-driven optimization results closely agreed with the experimentally validated surfactin titer of 5.75 ± 0.09 g L–1, demonstrating high model reliability and predictive accuracy. Our experimental design approach, integrated with machine-learning-driven optimization using limited experimental data, can be adopted across various bioprocess sectors to achieve substantial improvements in surfactin titer.

papers.title: From Fast Surrogates to Credible Solvers: Verification, Validation, and Reliability of Neural Operators in Computational Mechanics
papers.abstract: Neural operators, including Fourier neural operators, deep operator networks, graph- and geometry-based operators, wavelet operators, and physics-informed variants, are increasingly promoted as fast alternatives or complements to classical solvers for the Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) of computational mechanics. The supporting evidence, however, is still dominated by low prediction error, inference-time speed-up, in-distribution interpolation, and visually convincing field reconstructions. These criteria are necessary but not sufficient to establish numerical credibility: a model used as an engineering solver must additionally be examined through consistency, stability, convergence, conservation, boundary condition fidelity, validation against reference solutions, calibrated uncertainty, robustness under physically meaningful distribution shift, honest accuracy-matched cost, and reproducibility. This review reorganizes the neural operator literature around credibility rather than architecture or application. We introduce NO-CRED, a structured evidence framework with seven credibility dimensions and a five-level evidence ladder that assigns each study a transparent credibility profile rather than a single conflated score. NO-CRED translates established verification-and-validation practice to operator learning. Its specific additions are an operator-specific evidence ladder, a distribution shift dimension in which the applicability domain is defined by a training distribution rather than a solver’s fixed regime of validity, profile-based reporting justified by the weak coupling we measure between dimensions, and an executed auditable coding of the literature. We test the rubric used by the latter for stability; an intra-coder test–retest on a seed-selected subset of 14 studies gives per-dimension quadratic-weighted κ from 0.63 to 1.00, median 0.91, with all disagreements at adjacent levels, though no external double coding has been performed yet. Application to a curated released sample of 32 primary studies shows that within these 32 studies, the evidence is concentrated on accuracy. Uncertainty is absent in most (25/32), while genuine extrapolation (2/32) and accuracy-matched cost (3/32) are rare. Code is widely released (30/32), but full reproducibility is not (1/32). Strength on one dimension barely predicts strength on another. The sample supports a hypothesis that credibility appears to depend more on evaluation practice than on architecture, but more is needed before this can be proven. We assemble a failure mode atlas and an engineering-relevant taxonomy of distribution shift. In addition, we analyze when reported speed increases survive a fair accuracy-matched comparison with optimized classical and reduced-order methods. Finally, the paper closes with a credibility reporting checklist and a benchmark protocol.

papers.title: Prescribed‐Time Safe Actor–Critic Reinforcement Learning for Nonlinear Markov Jump Systems With Barrier‐Function Obstacle Avoidance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study studies generator‐assisted prescribed‐time safe actor–critic reinforcement learning for continuous‐time nonlinear Markov jump systems with boundary and obstacle constraints. A mode‐dependent critic approximates a Markov‐generator value function, and a mode‐dependent actor generates the nominal policy. Known or estimated nonlinear mode‐dependent dynamics are used in the control‐barrier‐function quadratic‐program safety filter, while generator information is used to form real‐state‐anchored virtual Bellman samples. Real online transitions and virtual samples are stored in a mode‐balanced replay buffer, which enriches mode‐wise updates without replacing the single realized trajectory. The running cost combines a bounded prescribed‐time weight with a two‐boundary barrier term, embedding deadline and safety information into value‐policy learning. The analysis combines the infinitesimal generator and Dynkin's formula between learning updates with explicit critic‐update jump bounds. The main result certifies practical prescribed‐time mean‐square uniform ultimate boundedness under an explicit generator condition based on the applied Bellman error. A nonlinear safe‐navigation simulation with unstable mode‐dependent dynamics validates deadline entry, obstacle avoidance, Markov switching, and the control‐demand tradeoff induced by different prescribed times.

papers.title: Pembelajaran Filtrasi Air untuk Membangun Literasi Lingkungan Siswa Kelas V MI: Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: This study examines how water filtration learning based on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) can support environmental literacy among fifth-grade Madrasah Ibtidaiyah students. It employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by collecting, screening, and analyzing scientific articles published from 2024 to 2026. The literature was analyzed descriptively and qualitatively to identify findings on water filtration experiments, environmental literacy, and ESD integration in elementary education. The results indicate that water filtration activities provide learning experiences through observation, experimentation, problem-solving, and discussion of clean water issues. These activities have the potential to develop four components of environmental literacy: environmental knowledge, attitudes, cognitive skills, and responsible behavior. Active learning models, including Problem-Based Learning, Project-Based Learning, and STEAM, can support student engagement and understanding. In conclusion, ESD-oriented water filtration learning offers a contextual approach to connecting science concepts with environmental awareness and responsibility. However, these findings require empirical testing in fifth-grade Madrasah Ibtidaiyah classrooms.
